title.en: Volume 57 Biographies 7: Pei Ji, Liu Wenjing

sentences.zh: ○溫大雅 子無隱　大雅弟彥博　子振　挺　大雅弟大有

translations.literal: Wen Daya; son Wuyin; Daya's younger brother Yanbo; sons Zhen and Ting; Daya's younger brother Dayou.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Daya; his son Wuyin; Daya's younger brother Yanbo; Yanbo's sons Zhen and Ting; and Daya's younger brother Dayou.

sentences.zh: 陳叔達　竇威子惲　兄子軌　軌子奉節　琮　從子抗　抗子衍　靜　靜子逵　誕　誕子孝慈孝慈子希玠　誕少子孝諶　抗季弟璡溫大雅溫大雅，字彥弘，太原祁人也。

translations.literal: Chen Shuda; Dou Wei and son Yun; nephew Gui; Gui's sons Fengjie and Cong; cousin Kang; Kang's sons Yan and Jing; Jing's son Kui; Dan; Dan's sons Xiaoci (Xiaoci's son Xijie) and Xiaoci's younger son Xiaochen; Kang's youngest brother Jin. Wen Daya. Wen Daya, styled Yanhong, was a native of Qi in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shuda; Dou Wei and his son Yun; Dou Wei's nephew Gui; Gui's sons Fengjie and Cong; Dou Wei's cousin Kang; Kang's sons Yan and Jing; Jing's son Kui; Dan; Dan's sons Xiaoci (whose son was Xijie) and Xiaoci's younger son Xiaochen; and Kang's youngest brother Jin. Wen Daya. Wen Daya, styled Yanhong, was a native of Qi in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 父君悠，北齊文林館學士，隋泗州司馬。

translations.literal: His father Junyou was a scholar of the Northern Qi's Wenslin Hall and served as Sui prefectural aide in Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Junyou had been a scholar in the Northern Qi's Wenslin Hall and later served as deputy prefect of Sizhou under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 大業末，為司隸從事，見隋政日亂，謝病而歸。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye reign, he served as an aide in the metropolitan inspectorate; seeing Sui government daily more chaotic, he pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Daye era he held a post in the metropolitan inspectorate, but as he watched Sui rule grow daily more chaotic, he pleaded illness and retired to his home.

sentences.zh: 大雅性至孝，少好學，以才辯知名。

translations.literal: Daya was by nature extremely filial, loved learning from youth, and was known for talent and eloquence.
translations.idiomatic: Daya was profoundly filial by nature, devoted himself to learning from an early age, and won renown for his talent and eloquence.

sentences.zh: 仕隋東宮學士、長安縣尉，以父憂去職。

translations.literal: He served the Sui as Eastern Palace academician and magistrate of Chang'an county, then left office on his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui he served as an academician in the crown prince's palace and as magistrate of Chang'an County, then resigned when his father died.

sentences.zh: 後以天下方亂，不求仕進。

translations.literal: Later, because the realm was in turmoil, he sought no further advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, with the empire falling into chaos, he made no effort to pursue office.

sentences.zh: 高祖鎮太原，甚禮之。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was stationed at Taiyuan, he treated Daya with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Gaozu was posted to Taiyuan, he treated Daya with exceptional respect.

sentences.zh: 義兵起，引為大將軍府記室參軍，專掌文翰。

translations.literal: When the righteous army rose, he was brought in as recorder of the great general's headquarters, in sole charge of documents.
translations.idiomatic: When the uprising began, Daya was appointed recorder on the great general's staff and put in sole charge of written communications.

sentences.zh: 禪代之際，與司錄竇威、主簿陳叔達參定禮儀。

translations.literal: At the time of the abdication and succession, together with registrar Dou Wei and chief clerk Chen Shuda he helped fix the ritual protocols.
translations.idiomatic: At the transfer of the throne he worked with Registrar Dou Wei and Chief Clerk Chen Shuda to establish the ceremonial protocols.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，歷遷黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude he was promoted through several posts to vice director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 618 he rose through several posts to become vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 弟彥博，為中書侍郎；

translations.literal: His younger brother Yanbo served as vice director of the Chancellery;
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yanbo served as vice director of the Chancellery;

sentences.zh: 對居近密，議者榮之。

translations.literal: the two faced each other in close confidential posts, and commentators regarded it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: the two brothers held neighboring posts at the heart of government, and contemporaries regarded their rise as a family triumph.

sentences.zh: 高祖從容謂曰：「我起義晉陽，為卿一門耳。」

translations.literal: Gaozu said at ease to him: "I raised the righteous army at Jinyang for your whole clan alone."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said to him in an easy tone, "When I raised the army at Jinyang, it was for your whole family."

sentences.zh: 尋轉工部，進拜陝東道大行台工部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to the Ministry of Works and advanced to Minister of Works on the Shandong Grand March route.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was transferred to the Ministry of Works and promoted to Minister of Works on the Shandong Grand March route.

sentences.zh: 太宗以隱太子、巢刺王之故，令大雅鎮洛陽以俟變。

translations.literal: Because of the Hidden Crown Prince and Prince of Chao and Ci, Taizong had Daya garrison Luoyang to await developments.
translations.idiomatic: On account of the conflict involving the Hidden Crown Prince and Prince of Chao and Ci, Taizong stationed Daya at Luoyang to watch for any turn of events.

sentences.zh: 大雅數陳秘策，甚蒙嘉賞。

translations.literal: Daya repeatedly presented secret stratagems and was greatly rewarded with praise.
translations.idiomatic: Daya repeatedly offered confidential counsel and won high praise for it.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，累轉禮部尚書，封黎國公。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, Daya was promoted through several posts to Minister of Rites and enfeoffed as Duke of Li.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong's accession, Daya rose through several posts to Minister of Rites and was enfeoffed as Duke of Li.

sentences.zh: 大雅將改葬其祖父，筮者曰：「葬於此地，害兄而福弟。」

translations.literal: When Daya was about to rebury his grandfather, the diviner said: "If buried in this place, it harms the elder brother and blesses the younger brother."
translations.idiomatic: When Daya was preparing to rebury his grandfather, the diviner said, "Burial in this spot will harm the elder brother and bring fortune to the younger."

sentences.zh: 大雅曰：「若得家弟永康，我將含笑入地。」

translations.literal: Daya said: "If my younger brother at home may enjoy lasting peace, I shall enter the earth with a smile."
translations.idiomatic: Daya replied, "If my younger brother may live in lasting health, I shall go to my grave with a smile."

sentences.zh: 葬訖，歲余而卒，謚曰孝。

translations.literal: After the burial was completed, a little more than a year later he died; his posthumous title was Filial.
translations.idiomatic: The burial was completed, and a little more than a year later he died; he was given the posthumous title Filial.

sentences.zh: 撰《創業起居注》三卷。

translations.literal: He compiled three fascicles of the 《Record of the Founding Court》.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote three fascicles of the 《Record of the Founding Court》.

sentences.zh: 永徽五年，贈尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yonghui he was posthumously made right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 654 he was posthumously appointed right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 子無隱，官至工部侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Wuyin reached the post of vice minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wuyin rose to the post of vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 大雅弟彥博。

translations.literal: Daya's younger brother Yanbo.
translations.idiomatic: Daya's younger brother was Yanbo.

sentences.zh: 弟 彥博彥博幼聰悟，有口辯，涉獵書記。

translations.literal: Younger brother Yanbo. Yanbo was clever and perceptive from childhood, had a gift for debate, and read widely in books and records.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yanbo. From childhood Yanbo was quick-witted, eloquent in debate, and widely read in books and records.

sentences.zh: 初，其父友薛道衡、李綱常見彥博兄弟三人，咸嘆異曰：「皆卿相才也。」

translations.literal: Earlier, his father's friends Xue Daoheng and Li Gang often saw the three Yanbo brothers and all sighed in wonder, saying: "Each is minister-and-chancellor material."
translations.idiomatic: Early on, his father's friends Xue Daoheng and Li Gang often met the three Yanbo brothers and each time marveled, saying, "Every one of them has the makings of a chief minister."

sentences.zh: 開皇末，為州牧秦孝王俊所薦，授文林郎，直內史省，轉通直謁者。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaihuang he was recommended by the prefectural governor Prince Qin Xiaojun, appointed gentleman of the Forest of Literature, served in the Secretariat, and was transferred to attendant for direct audience.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Kaihuang era he was recommended by Prince Qin Xiaojun, the prefectural governor, and appointed gentleman of the Forest of Literature; he served in the Secretariat and was later transferred to attendant for direct audience.

sentences.zh: 及隋亂，幽州總管羅藝引為司馬。

translations.literal: When the Sui fell into disorder, Youzhou regional inspector Luo Yi brought him in as aide.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sui empire collapsed into chaos, Luo Yi, regional inspector of Youzhou, took him on as his aide.

sentences.zh: 藝以幽州歸國，彥博贊成其事，授幽州總管府長史。

translations.literal: When Yi submitted Youzhou to the new state, Yanbo helped accomplish the matter and was appointed chief clerk of the Youzhou headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Luo Yi surrendered Youzhou to the Tang cause, Yanbo helped bring the submission about and was appointed chief clerk of the Youzhou headquarters.

sentences.zh: 未幾，征為中書舍人，俄遷中書侍郎，封西河郡公。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned as drafter of the Chancellery, soon promoted to vice director of the Chancellery, and enfeoffed as Duke of Xihe commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was summoned to serve as drafter in the Chancellery, soon promoted to vice director of the Chancellery, and enfeoffed as Duke of Xihe.

sentences.zh: 時高麗遣使貢方物，高祖謂群臣曰：「名實之間，理須相副。

translations.literal: At that time Goguryeo sent envoys with tribute goods; Gaozu said to the assembled ministers: "Between name and reality there must by right be correspondence.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Goguryeo sent envoys bearing tribute, and Gaozu told the assembled ministers, "Titles and realities ought to match one another.

sentences.zh: 高麗稱臣於隋，終拒煬帝，此亦何臣之有？

translations.literal: Goguryeo called itself a vassal of the Sui yet in the end defied Emperor Yang—what sort of vassal is that?
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo called itself a vassal of the Sui, yet in the end defied Emperor Yang—what kind of vassalage is that?

sentences.zh: 朕敬於萬物，不欲驕貴，但據土宇，務共安人，何必令其稱臣以自尊大？

translations.literal: I respect all things and do not wish arrogant elevation; I only hold the realm and strive together to settle the people—why must I make them call themselves vassals to aggrandize myself?
translations.idiomatic: I hold all under heaven in respect and do not wish to exalt myself through arrogance; I hold the realm only to bring peace to the people—why must I demand that they call themselves my vassals merely to puff up my own dignity?

sentences.zh: 可即為詔，述朕此懷也。」

translations.literal: You may at once draft an edict stating this intent of mine."
translations.idiomatic: Draft an edict at once and set forth this intention of mine."

sentences.zh: 彥博進曰：「遼東之地，周為箕子之國，漢家之玄菟郡耳。

translations.literal: Yanbo advanced and said: "The land of Liaodong was in Zhou the state of Jizi and in Han merely the commandery of Xuantu.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo stepped forward and said, "The land of Liaodong was in Zhou the domain of Jizi, and under the Han it was merely the commandery of Xuantu.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉已前，近在提封之內，不可許以不臣。

translations.literal: Before Wei and Jin it lay within our very borders; one cannot permit it not to be a vassal.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Wei and Jin dynasties it lay well within our borders; we cannot allow it to stand outside vassal status.

sentences.zh: 若與高麗抗禮，則四夷何以瞻仰？

translations.literal: If we treat Goguryeo as an equal in ritual, how will the four barbarians look up to us?
translations.idiomatic: If we treat Goguryeo as an equal in ceremony, what will the four quarters of the barbarian world have to look up to?

sentences.zh: 且中國之於夷狄，猶太陽之比列星，理無降尊，俯同夷貊。」

translations.literal: Moreover China toward the barbarians is like the sun toward the lesser stars; by right there is no lowering of dignity to bow level with the barbarian borderlands."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, China's relation to the barbarians is like that of the sun to the lesser stars; by right there is no lowering of dignity to stoop to their level."

sentences.zh: 高祖乃止。

translations.literal: Gaozu thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu thereupon abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 其年，突厥入寇，命右衛大將軍張瑾為并州道行軍總管，出拒之，以彥博為行軍長史。

translations.literal: That year the Turks invaded; he ordered right guard general Zhang Jin to be campaign commander of the Bingzhou route to go out and resist, with Yanbo as campaign chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: That year, when the Turks invaded, he appointed Zhang Jin, general of the right guard, campaign commander of the Bingzhou route to meet them, with Yanbo as his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 與虜戰於太谷，軍敗，彥博沒於虜庭。

translations.literal: They fought the enemy at Taigu; the army was defeated and Yanbo was lost in the barbarian court.
translations.idiomatic: They fought the enemy at Taigu; the army was defeated and Yanbo fell into Turkic hands.

sentences.zh: 突厥以其近臣，苦問以國家虛實及兵馬多少，彥博固不肯言。

translations.literal: Because he was a close minister of the Turks, they pressed him hard on the state's strength and weakness and the number of troops and horses; Yanbo firmly refused to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had been a high minister at court, the Turks pressed him relentlessly about the empire's strengths and weaknesses and the size of its armies; Yanbo steadfastly refused to answer.

sentences.zh: 頡利怒，遷於陰山苦塞之地。

translations.literal: Jieli was angry and moved him to the bitter frontier lands of the Yin Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli flew into a rage and exiled him to the harsh frontier country of the Yin Mountains.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，突厥送款，始征彥博還朝，授雍州治中，尋檢校吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne the Turks sent tokens of submission; only then was Yanbo summoned back to court, appointed administrator of Yongzhou, and soon made acting vice director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong's accession the Turks submitted, and only then was Yanbo summoned back to court; he was appointed administrator of Yongzhou and soon made acting vice director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 彥博意有沙汰，多所損抑，而退者不伏，囂訟盈庭。

translations.literal: Yanbo intended to sift and purge, and greatly reduced and suppressed many; those demoted would not submit, and clamorous lawsuits filled the court.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo set out to weed out unfit officials and demoted many of them; those he removed refused to accept their demotions, and the court was filled with noisy appeals.

sentences.zh: 彥博惟騁辭辯，與之相詰，終日喧擾，頗為識者所嗤。

translations.literal: Yanbo only unleashed his eloquence and cross-examined them; all day there was uproar, and men of insight largely scoffed at him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo relied solely on his gift for argument, debating them point by point until the hall rang all day with uproar—a spectacle that thoughtful observers largely ridiculed.

sentences.zh: 復拜中書侍郎，兼太子右庶子。

translations.literal: He was again appointed vice director of the Chancellery and concurrently right vice guardian of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed vice director of the Chancellery and concurrently right vice guardian of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二年，遷御史大夫，仍檢校中書侍郎事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenguan he was moved to censor-in-chief while still acting in the affairs of vice director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In 628 he was promoted to censor-in-chief while continuing to act as vice director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 彥博善於宣吐，每奉使入朝，詔問四方風俗，承受綸言，有若成誦。

translations.literal: Yanbo was skilled at public delivery; whenever he came to court on mission and was questioned by edict on customs of the four quarters, he received the imperial words as if they were already memorized.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo was a master of public speech; whenever he came to court on embassy and was questioned by edict about customs across the realm, he received the emperor's words and answered as though he had memorized them in advance.

sentences.zh: 聲韻高朗，響溢殿庭，進止雍容，觀者拭目。

translations.literal: His tone was high and clear, his voice overflowed the hall, his comings and goings were composed and easy, and onlookers wiped their eyes.
translations.idiomatic: His voice rang clear and high, filling the hall; his bearing as he advanced and withdrew was dignified and graceful, and those who watched could only stare in admiration.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷中書令，進爵虞國公。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was moved to director of the Chancellery and advanced in rank to Duke of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: In 630 he was promoted to director of the Chancellery and raised in rank to Duke of Yu.

sentences.zh: 高祖常宴朝臣，詔太宗諭旨，既而顧謂近臣曰：「何如溫彥博？」

translations.literal: Gaozu often feasted the court ministers and ordered Taizong to convey the imperial intent; then he turned to the close ministers and said: "How does Wen Yanbo compare?"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu often entertained the court ministers and had Taizong convey the imperial message; then he would turn to those nearest him and ask, "How does Wen Yanbo compare?"

sentences.zh: 其見重如此。

translations.literal: Thus was he valued.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 初，突厥之降也，詔議安邊之術。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Turks submitted, an edict ordered discussion of methods to secure the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Turks submitted, the court was ordered to debate how best to secure the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 朝士多言：「突厥恃強，擾亂中國，為日久矣。

translations.literal: Many at court said: "The Turks have relied on strength and disturbed China for a long time already.
translations.idiomatic: Many at court argued, "The Turks have long relied on their strength to harass China.

sentences.zh: 今天實喪之，窮來歸我，本非慕義之心也。

translations.literal: Now Heaven has truly abandoned them; in destitution they come to submit to us—it is fundamentally not a heart that admires righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has now truly forsaken them; they come to us in desperation, not out of any genuine regard for our virtue.

sentences.zh: 因其歸命，分其種落，俘之河南，散屬州縣，各使耕田，變其風俗。

translations.literal: Taking advantage of their submission, divide their tribes, move them captive south of the Yellow River, scatter them among prefectures and counties, have each plow fields, and change their customs.
translations.idiomatic: We should take advantage of their submission to break up their tribes, move them south of the Yellow River, scatter them among the prefectures and counties, set them to farming, and transform their ways.

sentences.zh: 百萬胡虜，可得化而為漢，則中國有加戶之利，塞北常空矣。」

translations.literal: A million barbarian captives could be transformed into Han; then China would gain households and the northern frontier would stand forever empty."
translations.idiomatic: A million barbarian captives could be transformed into Han subjects; China would gain households, and the northern frontier would stand forever empty."

sentences.zh: 惟彥博議曰：「漢建武時，置降匈奴於五原塞下，全其部落，得為捍蔽，又不離其土俗，因而撫之。

translations.literal: Only Yanbo argued: "In the Jianwu era of Han, surrendered Xiongnu were placed below the Wuyuan pass, their tribes kept whole so they could serve as a shield, and without leaving their native customs they were thereby comforted.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yanbo argued, "Under Emperor Guangwu of Han, surrendered Xiongnu were settled below the Wuyuan pass; their tribes were kept intact so they could serve as a frontier shield, and without uprooting their native customs they were governed where they lived.

sentences.zh: 一則實空虛之地，二則示無猜之心。

translations.literal: First, it would fill empty lands; second, it would show a heart free of suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: That would both populate empty frontier lands and demonstrate a policy free of suspicion.

sentences.zh: 若遣向西南，則乖物性，故非含育之道也。」

translations.literal: If sent toward the southwest, that would go against their nature—thus it is not the way of cherishing and nurturing."
translations.idiomatic: To send them southwest would go against their nature and would not be true nurturing governance."

sentences.zh: 太宗從之，遂處降人於朔方之地，其入居長安者近且萬家。

translations.literal: Taizong followed this; he thereupon settled the surrendered people in the Shuofang region, and those who entered and dwelt in Chang'an approached ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong accepted this view and settled the surrendered Turks in the Shuofang region; nearly ten thousand households of them took up residence in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 議者尤為不便，欲建突厥國於河外。

translations.literal: Those who debated found it especially inconvenient and wished to establish a Turkic state beyond the river.
translations.idiomatic: Critics found the arrangement especially troubling and wanted to establish a Turkic state beyond the river.

sentences.zh: 彥博又執奏曰：「既已納之，無故遣去，深為可惜。」

translations.literal: Yanbo again held firmly to memorial and said: "Since we have already received them, to send them away without cause would be deeply regrettable."
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo again submitted a firm memorial: "Now that we have taken them in, to send them away without cause would be a profound waste."

sentences.zh: 與魏徵等爭論，數年不決。

translations.literal: He disputed with Wei Zheng and others for several years without resolution.
translations.idiomatic: He debated the matter with Wei Zheng and others for years without a final decision.

sentences.zh: 十年，遷尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was moved to right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 636 he was promoted to right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 明年薨，年六十四。

translations.literal: The next year he died; he was sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he died at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 彥博自掌知機務，即杜絕賓客，國之利害，知無不言，太宗以是嘉之。

translations.literal: From the time Yanbo took charge of confidential affairs he cut off guests; on the state's benefit and harm he spoke whenever he knew—Taizong for this praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yanbo took charge of state secrets he cut off social visits entirely; on every matter of national consequence he spoke his mind without reserve, and Taizong prized him for it.

sentences.zh: 及薨，謂侍臣曰：「彥博以憂國之故，勞精竭神，我見其不逮，已二年矣。

translations.literal: When he died, he said to the attending ministers: "Yanbo, for the sake of worrying over the state, exhausted his spirit and strength; I saw him no longer equal to it already two years ago.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanbo died, Taizong told his attendants, "Yanbo wore himself out worrying over the state; I had seen him failing for two years already.

sentences.zh: 恨不縱其閒逸，致夭性靈。」

translations.literal: I regret that I did not allow him leisure and ease, causing his natural spirit to die young."
translations.idiomatic: I regret that I did not give him more leisure and thereby cut short his life."

sentences.zh: 彥博家無正寢，及卒之日，殯於別室，太宗命有司為造堂焉。

translations.literal: Yanbo's household had no proper main chamber; on the day he died the coffin lay in a side room, and Taizong ordered the relevant offices to build a hall for them.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo's household had no proper main hall; when he died the coffin lay in a side room, and Taizong ordered the authorities to build one for the family.

sentences.zh: 贈特進，謚曰恭，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made specially advanced; his posthumous title was Respectful, and he was buried with honor at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed specially advanced, given the posthumous title Respectful, and buried with honor at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 子振，少有雅望，官至太子舍人，居喪以毀卒。

translations.literal: His son Zhen had an elegant reputation from youth, reached the post of crown prince attendant, and died in mourning from grief-induced ruin of health.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhen enjoyed a fine reputation from youth, rose to crown prince attendant, and died in mourning when grief ruined his health.

sentences.zh: 振弟挺，尚高祖女千金公主，官至延州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhen's younger brother Ting married Gaozu's daughter Princess Qianjin and reached the post of prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's younger brother Ting married Gaozu's daughter Princess Qianjin and rose to prefect of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 弟 大有大雅弟大有，字彥將，性端謹，少以學行稱。

translations.literal: Younger brother Dayou. Daya's younger brother Dayou, styled Yanjiang, was by nature upright and careful and was known from youth for learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Dayou. Daya's younger brother Dayou, styled Yanjiang, was upright and careful by nature and was known from youth for his learning and conduct.

sentences.zh: 隋仁壽中，尚書右丞李綱表薦之，授羽騎尉。

translations.literal: In the Renshou era of Sui, right vice director of the Department of State Affairs Li Gang memorialized to recommend him, and he was appointed captain of feathered riders.
translations.idiomatic: During the Renshou era of the Sui, Li Gang, right vice director of the Department of State Affairs, recommended him by memorial, and he was appointed captain of the feathered riders.

sentences.zh: 尋丁憂去，職歸鄉里。

translations.literal: Soon he left on his mother's death and returned his post to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he resigned on his mother's death and returned home.

sentences.zh: 義旗初舉，高祖引為太原令。

translations.literal: When the righteous banner was first raised, Gaozu brought him in as magistrate of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the uprising first began, Gaozu appointed him magistrate of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 從太宗擊西河，高祖謂曰：「士馬尚少，要資經略，以卿參謀軍事，其善建功名也！

translations.literal: Following Taizong in the attack on Xihe, Gaozu said to him: "Troops and horses are still few; we need planning and strategy—take you to advise on military affairs and build merit well!
translations.idiomatic: When he followed Taizong in the attack on Xihe, Gaozu told him, "Our forces are still few and we need sound strategy; serve as military adviser on this campaign and win yourself a name!

sentences.zh: 事之成敗，當以此行卜之。

translations.literal: Success or failure of the affair should be divined by this campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Whether our enterprise succeeds or fails will be foretold by this campaign.

sentences.zh: 若克西河，帝業成矣。」

translations.literal: If Xihe is taken, the imperial enterprise is accomplished."
translations.idiomatic: If we take Xihe, the imperial enterprise is assured."

sentences.zh: 及破西河而還，復以本官攝大將軍府記室，與兄大雅共掌機密。

translations.literal: When Xihe was broken and they returned, he again held his former post in charge of the great general's recorder, and together with his elder brother Daya managed confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Xihe fell and they returned, he again served in his former capacity as recorder on the great general's staff, sharing confidential affairs with his elder brother Daya.

sentences.zh: 大有以昆季同在機務，意不自安，固請他職。

translations.literal: Dayou, because brothers together were in confidential posts, felt ill at ease and firmly requested another office.
translations.idiomatic: Dayou felt uneasy that both brothers held posts at the heart of government and firmly asked for a different assignment.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「我虛心相待，不以為疑，卿何自疑也？」

translations.literal: Gaozu said: "I treat you with an open heart and do not regard you with suspicion—why do you suspect yourself?"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "I receive you with an open heart and harbor no suspicion—why do you suspect yourself?"

sentences.zh: 大有雖應命，然每退讓，遠避機權，僚列以此多之。

translations.literal: Dayou though he accepted the command yet each time yielded, keeping far from the levers of power; colleagues for this praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Dayou accepted the appointment, yet he always yielded ground and kept his distance from power; his colleagues admired him for it.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，累轉中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude he was promoted through several posts to vice director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In 618 he rose through several posts to vice director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 會卒，高祖甚傷惜之，贈鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: He happened to die; Gaozu deeply grieved and regretted it and posthumously made him director of the Court for Dependencies.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward; Gaozu grieved deeply and posthumously appointed him director of the Court for Dependencies.

sentences.zh: 初，大雅在隋，與顏思魯俱在東宮，彥博與思魯弟愍楚同直內史省，彥將與愍楚弟游秦典校秘閣。

translations.literal: Earlier, Daya under the Sui was together with Yan Silu in the Eastern Palace; Yanbo was together with Silu's younger brother Mintu on duty in the Secretariat; Yanjiang together with Mintu's younger brother Youqin managed collation in the secret archive.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, under the Sui, Daya had served with Yan Silu in the crown prince's palace; Yanbo had served with Silu's younger brother Mintu in the Secretariat; and Yanjiang had worked with Mintu's younger brother Youqin collating texts in the imperial archive.

sentences.zh: 二家兄弟，各為一時人物之選。

translations.literal: The brothers of the two families were each chosen men of their time.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers of both families were among the leading figures of their generation.

sentences.zh: 少時學業，顏氏為優；

translations.literal: In youth for scholarly achievement the Yan clan was superior;
translations.idiomatic: In their youth the Yan brothers were superior in scholarship;

sentences.zh: 其後職位，溫氏為盛。

translations.literal: afterward in office the Wen clan was flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: but afterward the Wen clan rose higher in office.

sentences.zh: 陳叔達，字子聰，陳宣帝第十六子也。

translations.literal: Chen Shuda, styled Zicong, was the sixteenth son of Emperor Xuan of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shuda, styled Zicong, was the sixteenth son of Emperor Xuan of Chen.

sentences.zh: 善容止，頗有才學，在陳封義陽王。

translations.literal: He was skilled in bearing and deportment, had considerable talent and learning, and under Chen was enfeoffed as Prince of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was graceful in bearing, possessed considerable talent and learning, and under the Chen was enfeoffed as Prince of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 年十餘歲，嘗侍宴，賦詩十韻，援筆便就，僕射徐陵甚奇之。

translations.literal: At a little more than ten years he once attended a feast, composed a poem in ten rhymes, took up the brush and finished at once; vice director Xu Ling greatly marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: When he was barely more than ten, he once attended a feast and composed a ten-rhyme poem at a stroke; Vice Director Xu Ling was deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 歷侍中、丹陽尹、都官尚書。

translations.literal: He successively served as attendant-in-ordinary, governor of Danyang, and minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as attendant-in-ordinary, governor of Danyang, and minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 入隋，久不得調。

translations.literal: Entering the Sui, for a long time he received no transfer.
translations.idiomatic: After the Chen fell and he entered Sui service, he long went without a new appointment.

sentences.zh: 大業中，拜內史舍人，出為絳郡通守。

translations.literal: In the Daye era he was appointed drafter of the Secretariat and went out as transit governor of Jiang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era he was appointed drafter in the Secretariat and then sent out as transit governor of Jiang commandery.

sentences.zh: 義師至絳郡，叔達以郡歸款，授丞相府主簿，封漢東郡公。

translations.literal: When the righteous army reached Jiang commandery, Shuda submitted the commandery in allegiance, was appointed chief clerk of the chancellor's office, and enfeoffed as Duke of Handong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the uprising reached Jiang commandery, Shuda surrendered the district and was appointed chief clerk in the chancellor's office and enfeoffed as Duke of Handong.

sentences.zh: 與記室溫大雅同掌機密，軍書、赦令及禪代文誥，多叔達所為。

translations.literal: Together with recorder Wen Daya he managed confidential affairs; military documents, amnesties, and the abdication and succession proclamations were largely Shuda's work.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Recorder Wen Daya he managed confidential affairs; military dispatches, amnesties, and the documents of abdication and succession were largely Shuda's work.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，授黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude he was appointed vice director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 618 he was appointed vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二年，兼納言。

translations.literal: In the second year he was concurrently made remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: In 619 he was also appointed remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 四年，拜侍中。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: In 621 he was appointed attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 叔達明辯，善容止，每有敷奏，搢紳莫不屬目。

translations.literal: Shuda was clear in argument and skilled in bearing; whenever he presented memorials, the gentry all fixed their eyes on him.
translations.idiomatic: Shuda was sharp in debate and graceful in bearing; whenever he addressed the throne, the court elite watched him with rapt attention.

sentences.zh: 江南名士薄游長安者，多為薦拔。

translations.literal: Famous scholars of the south who briefly traveled to Chang'an were mostly recommended and promoted by him.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended and advanced many distinguished scholars from the south who had come to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 五年，進封江國公。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: In 622 he was raised in rank to Duke of Jiang.

sentences.zh: 嘗賜食於御前，得蒲萄，執而不食。

translations.literal: He was once granted food before the emperor and received grapes, which he held but did not eat.
translations.idiomatic: Once, when he was served food in the emperor's presence, he was given grapes but held them without eating.

sentences.zh: 高祖問其故，對曰：「臣母患口乾，求之不能致，欲歸以遺母。」

translations.literal: Gaozu asked the reason; he replied: "My mother suffers from dry mouth; I could not obtain these though I sought them—I wish to take them home as a gift for my mother."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu asked why, and he answered, "My mother suffers from dry mouth. I could not obtain grapes for her, and I wish to take these home for her."

sentences.zh: 高祖喟然流涕曰：「卿有母遺乎！」

translations.literal: Gaozu sighed with tears and said: "You still have a mother to present gifts to!"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sighed with tears and said, "You still have a mother to care for!"

sentences.zh: 因賜物三百段。

translations.literal: He thereupon bestowed three hundred bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: He then bestowed three hundred bolts of goods on him.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，加授光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was additionally appointed grand master for splendid happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan era he was additionally appointed grand master for splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 尋坐與蕭瑀對御忿爭免官。

translations.literal: Soon he was dismissed from office for quarreling angrily with Xiao Yu before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was dismissed for quarreling angrily with Xiao Yu in the emperor's presence.

sentences.zh: 未幾，丁母憂。

translations.literal: Before long he entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his mother died and he entered mourning.

sentences.zh: 叔達先有疾，太宗慮其危殆，遣使禁絕吊賓。

translations.literal: Shuda had long been ill; Taizong feared he was in peril and sent envoys to forbid condolence visitors.
translations.idiomatic: Shuda had long been ill, and Taizong, fearing for his life, sent orders forbidding visitors from coming to offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 服闋，授遂州都督，以疾不行。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed regional inspector of Suizhou but did not take up the post because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended he was appointed regional inspector of Suizhou, but illness kept him from taking up the post.

sentences.zh: 久之，拜禮部尚書。

translations.literal: After a long time he was appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 建成、元吉嫉害太宗，陰行譖毀，高祖惑其言，將有貶責，叔達固諫乃止。

translations.literal: Jiancheng and Yuanji envied and harmed Taizong, secretly slandering him; Gaozu was swayed by their words and was about to demote and rebuke him, but Shuda firmly remonstrated and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: Jiancheng and Yuanji envied Taizong and secretly slandered him; Gaozu was taken in by their words and was about to punish Taizong, but Shuda remonstrated firmly and stopped it.

sentences.zh: 至是太宗勞之曰：「武德時，危難潛構，知公有讜言，今之此拜，有以相答。」

translations.literal: At this time Taizong comforted him, saying: "In the Wude era peril was secretly forming; I knew you had forthright counsel—this present appointment is my answer."
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion Taizong thanked him, saying, "During the Wude era danger was brewing in secret, and I knew you spoke forthright counsel. This appointment is my answer to you."

sentences.zh: 叔達謝曰：「此不獨為陛下，社稷計耳。」

translations.literal: Shuda thanked him and said: "This was not only for Your Majesty—it was for the altars of state."
translations.idiomatic: Shuda replied, "I did that not for Your Majesty alone, but for the sake of the realm."

sentences.zh: 後坐閨庭不理，為憲司所劾。

translations.literal: Later he was impeached by the censorate for neglecting his household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was impeached by the censorate for neglecting his official duties at home.

sentences.zh: 朝廷惜其名臣，不欲彰其罪，聽以散秩歸第。

translations.literal: The court valued this famous minister and did not wish to display his crime; he was permitted to return home on a nominal salary.
translations.idiomatic: The court valued so distinguished a minister and did not wish to publicize his offense; he was allowed to retire home on a nominal stipend.

sentences.zh: 九年卒，謚曰繆。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died; his posthumous title was Erring.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 635; his posthumous title was Erring.

sentences.zh: 後贈戶部尚書，改謚曰忠。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously made Minister of Revenue and his posthumous title was changed to Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: He was later posthumously appointed Minister of Revenue, and his posthumous title was changed to Loyal.

sentences.zh: 有集十五卷。

translations.literal: He left a collected works in fifteen fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected works in fifteen fascicles.

sentences.zh: 竇威竇威，字文蔚，扶風平陸人，太穆皇后從父兄也。

translations.literal: Dou Wei. Dou Wei, styled Wenwei, was a native of Pinglu in Fufeng and a paternal cousin of the Grand Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wei. Dou Wei, styled Wenwei, was a native of Pinglu in Fufeng and a paternal cousin of the Grand Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 父熾，隋太傅。

translations.literal: His father Chi was Sui grand tutor.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chi had served as grand tutor under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 威家世勳貴，諸昆弟並尚武藝，而威耽玩文史，介然自守。

translations.literal: Wei's family for generations had been meritorious and noble; all his brothers prized martial arts, but Wei immersed himself in literature and history and kept himself aloof.
translations.idiomatic: The Dou family had long been eminent for merit and rank; all his brothers prized martial skill, but Wei devoted himself to literature and history and held himself apart.

sentences.zh: 諸兄哂之，謂為「書痴」。

translations.literal: His elder brothers mocked him and called him a "book fool."
translations.idiomatic: His brothers mocked him and called him a "book fool."

sentences.zh: 隋內史令李德林舉秀異，射策甲科，拜秘書郎。

translations.literal: Sui director of the Secretariat Li Delin recommended him as outstanding talent; in the archery examination he took first class and was appointed secretary gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Li Delin, director of the Secretariat under the Sui, recommended him as outstanding talent; he took first place in the civil examination and was appointed secretary gentleman.

sentences.zh: 秩滿當遷，而固守不調，在秘書十餘歲，其學業益廣。

translations.literal: When his term was full he should have been transferred, but he firmly held to no transfer; in the Secretariat for more than ten years his learning grew ever broader.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he was due for promotion, but he steadfastly refused transfer; he remained in the Secretariat for more than ten years, and his learning grew ever broader.

sentences.zh: 時諸兄並以軍功致仕通顯，交結豪貴，賓客盈門，而威職掌閒散。

translations.literal: At that time all his brothers through military merit reached prominent office, formed ties with powerful nobles, and had guests filling their gates, while Wei held a leisurely and minor post.
translations.idiomatic: At that time all his brothers had risen to prominence through military merit, cultivated ties with powerful nobles, and kept their gates crowded with guests, while Wei held a minor and undemanding post.

sentences.zh: 諸兄更謂威曰：「昔孔子積學成聖，猶狼狽當時，棲遲若此，汝效此道，復欲何求？

translations.literal: His brothers again said to Wei: "In the past Confucius accumulated learning and became a sage, yet was still in distress in his own time and delayed like this—if you imitate this path, what more do you seek?
translations.idiomatic: His brothers said to him again, "Confucius piled up learning until he became a sage, yet even he was hard pressed in his own day and lingered in obscurity as you do. If you follow that path, what more do you expect?

sentences.zh: 名位不達，固其宜矣。」

translations.literal: That fame and position do not arrive is surely fitting."
translations.idiomatic: That you should fail to win rank and renown is only fitting."

sentences.zh: 威笑而不答。

translations.literal: Wei smiled and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Wei smiled and made no reply.

sentences.zh: 久之，蜀王秀闢為記室，以秀行事多不法，稱疾還田裡。

translations.literal: After a long time Prince of Shu Xiu summoned him as recorder; because Xiu's conduct was largely unlawful, he pleaded illness and returned to his fields.
translations.idiomatic: After some time Prince Xiu of Shu summoned him as recorder, but because the prince's conduct was often unlawful, Wei pleaded illness and returned to his home estate.

sentences.zh: 及秀廢黜，府僚多獲罪，唯威以先見保全。

translations.literal: When Xiu was deposed and dismissed, many staff of his princely establishment were punished; only Wei, through foresight, was preserved.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xiu was deposed, many of his staff were punished, but Wei alone escaped harm because he had withdrawn in time.

sentences.zh: 大業四年，累遷內史舍人，以數陳得失忤旨，轉考功郎中，後坐事免，歸京師。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daye he was promoted through several posts to drafter of the Secretariat; because he repeatedly stated gains and losses and offended the imperial intent, he was transferred to director of merit in the Ministry of Personnel, later dismissed for an offense, and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In 608 he rose through several posts to drafter in the Secretariat; because he repeatedly criticized policy and offended the throne, he was transferred to director of merit in the Ministry of Personnel, later dismissed for an offense, and returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 高祖入關，召補大丞相府司錄參軍。

translations.literal: When Gaozu entered the passes he was summoned to fill the post of registrar of the great chancellor's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu entered the passes, Wei was summoned to serve as registrar on the great chancellor's staff.

sentences.zh: 時軍旅草創，五禮曠墜。

translations.literal: At that time the army was newly formed and the five rites lay in ruin.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the army was still being organized and the five rites lay in ruins.

sentences.zh: 威既博物，多識舊儀，朝章國典，皆其所定，禪代文翰多參預焉。

translations.literal: Wei was broadly learned and knew many old protocols; court regulations and state statutes were all set by him, and he largely took part in the documents of abdication and succession.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was broadly learned and knew the old protocols well; he established the court regulations and state statutes and took a leading part in drafting the documents of abdication and succession.

sentences.zh: 高祖常謂裴寂曰：「叔孫通不能加也。」

translations.literal: Gaozu often said to Pei Ji: "Shusun Tong could not surpass him."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu often told Pei Ji, "Shusun Tong himself could not have done better."

sentences.zh: 武德元年，拜內史令。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude he was appointed director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 618 he was appointed director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 威奏議雍容，多引古為諭，高祖甚親重之，或引入臥內，常為膝席。

translations.literal: Wei's memorials and deliberations were composed and easy; he often cited antiquity as illustration; Gaozu greatly favored and valued him, sometimes bringing him into the sleeping quarters and regularly seating him on the knee-cushion.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's memorials were measured and dignified, and he often drew on antiquity to make his points; Gaozu favored him deeply, sometimes received him in his private quarters, and regularly seated him on the knee-cushion beside him.

sentences.zh: 又嘗謂曰：「昔周朝有八柱國之貴，吾與公家咸登此職。

translations.literal: He also once said to him: "In the past the Zhou had the nobility of the eight pillar states; your house and mine both attained that office.
translations.idiomatic: He also once told him, "In the Zhou dynasty there were the eight pillar states; both your family and mine once held that rank.

sentences.zh: 今我已為天子，公為內史令，本同末異，乃不平矣。」

translations.literal: Now I am already Son of Heaven and you are director of the Secretariat—we were alike at the root but differ at the branch; this is indeed not level."
translations.idiomatic: Now I am emperor and you are director of the Secretariat. We began alike but have ended differently—surely that is no cause for resentment."

sentences.zh: 威謝曰：「臣家昔在漢朝，再為外戚，至於後魏，三處外家，陛下隆興，復出皇后。

translations.literal: Wei thanked him and said: "My house in the past under Han twice became affinal kin; down to the later Wei, three times it was an affinal house; Your Majesty's glorious rise again produced an empress.
translations.idiomatic: Wei replied, "In Han times my family twice became imperial affines; under the later Wei we were affines three times; and under Your Majesty's glorious rise an empress has again come from our house.

sentences.zh: 臣又階緣戚裡，位忝鳳池，自惟叨濫，曉夕兢懼。」

translations.literal: I again, by steps of affinal connection, hold a post unworthy of the Phoenix Pool; reflecting on my presumptuous excess, from dawn to dusk I am in fearful caution."
translations.idiomatic: I have risen through imperial kinship to a post I do not deserve at the heart of government, and I tremble day and night at my presumption."

sentences.zh: 高祖笑曰：「比見關東人與崔、盧為婚，猶自矜伐，公代為帝戚，不亦貴乎！」

translations.literal: Gaozu laughed and said: "Recently I have seen men east of the pass marry with the Cui and Lu clans and still boast themselves—your house for generations has been imperial affines—is that not even more noble!"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu laughed and said, "I have lately seen men east of the pass marry into the Cui and Lu clans and still boast of it—your house has been imperial kin for generations. Is that not nobler still?"

sentences.zh: 及寢疾，高祖自往臨問。

translations.literal: When he took to his bed ill, Gaozu himself went to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell gravely ill, Gaozu went in person to visit him.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，家無餘財，遺令薄葬。

translations.literal: Soon he died; the household had no surplus wealth, and his testament ordered a simple burial.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward, leaving his household without surplus wealth and ordering a simple burial in his will.

sentences.zh: 謚曰靖，贈同州刺史，追封延安郡公。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Tranquil; he was posthumously made prefect of Tongzhou and retroactively enfeoffed as Duke of Yan'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Tranquil, posthumously appointed prefect of Tongzhou, and retroactively enfeoffed as Duke of Yan'an.

sentences.zh: 葬日，詔太子及百官並出臨送。

translations.literal: On the day of burial, an edict ordered the crown prince and all officials to go out and attend the send-off.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his burial, the crown prince and all officials were ordered to attend the funeral.

sentences.zh: 有文集十捲。

translations.literal: He had a literary collection in ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left a literary collection in ten juan.

sentences.zh: 子惲嗣，官至岐州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Yun succeeded him and reached the post of prefect of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yun succeeded him and rose to prefect of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 威兄子軌，從兄子抗，並知名。

translations.literal: Wei's nephew Gui and cousin's son Kang were both well known.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's nephew Gui and his cousin's son Kang were both well known.

sentences.zh: 窦軌軌，字士則，周雍州牧、酂國公恭之子也。

translations.literal: Dou Gui. Gui, styled Shize, was son of Zhou regional inspector of Yongzhou and Duke of Zan Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Gui. Gui, styled Shize, was the son of Gong, regional inspector of Yongzhou under the Zhou and Duke of Zan.

sentences.zh: 隋大業中，為資陽郡東曹掾，後去官歸於家。

translations.literal: In the Daye era of Sui he was eastern bureau aide of Ziyang commandery, later left office and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era he served as eastern bureau aide in Ziyang commandery, then resigned and returned home.

sentences.zh: 義兵起，軌聚眾千餘人，迎謁於長春宮。

translations.literal: When the righteous army rose, Gui gathered more than a thousand men and went to pay respects at Changchun Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the uprising began, Gui gathered more than a thousand followers and went to Changchun Palace to pay his respects.

sentences.zh: 高祖見之，大悅，降席握手，語及平生，賜良馬十匹，使掠地渭南。

translations.literal: Gaozu saw him and was greatly pleased, came down from his seat to grasp his hand, spoke of their whole lives, bestowed ten fine horses, and sent him to seize territory south of the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was delighted to see him, rose from his seat to take his hand, spoke of their shared past, gave him ten fine horses, and sent him to secure territory south of the Wei River.

sentences.zh: 軌先下永豐倉，收兵得五千人。

translations.literal: Gui first took Yongfeng granary and gathered troops to five thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Gui first seized Yongfeng granary and raised a force of five thousand men.

sentences.zh: 從平京城，封贊皇縣公，拜大丞相諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Following in the pacification of the capital region, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Zanhuang county and appointed advisory staff officer of the great chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the pacification of the capital, was enfeoffed as Duke of Zanhuang, and appointed advisory staff officer on the great chancellor's staff.

sentences.zh: 時稽胡賊五萬餘人掠宜春，軌討之。

translations.literal: At that time more than fifty thousand Ji Hu bandits plundered Yichun; Gui campaigned against them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time more than fifty thousand Ji Hu raiders were plundering Yichun, and Gui was sent to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 行次黃欽山，與賊相遇，賊乘高縱火，王師稍卻。

translations.literal: Marching to Huangqin Mountain he met the bandits; the bandits took the high ground and set fires, and the imperial army slightly withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Marching to Huangqin Mountain he met the enemy; they held the high ground and set fires, and the imperial army fell back.

sentences.zh: 軌斬其部將十四人，拔隊中小帥以代之。

translations.literal: Gui beheaded fourteen of their subordinate generals and promoted junior commanders in the ranks to replace them.
translations.idiomatic: Gui beheaded fourteen of his own subordinate officers and promoted junior commanders from the ranks to replace them.

sentences.zh: 軌自率數百騎殿於軍後，令之曰：「聞鼓聲有不進者，自後斬之。」

translations.literal: Gui himself led several hundred horsemen as rearguard of the army and ordered them: "Whoever on hearing the drum does not advance will be beheaded from behind."
translations.idiomatic: Gui himself led several hundred horsemen as rearguard and ordered, "Anyone who fails to advance at the drum will be cut down from behind."

sentences.zh: 既聞鼓，士卒爭先赴敵，賊射之，不能止，因大破之，斬首千餘級，虜男女二萬口。

translations.literal: Once the drum was heard, soldiers vied to rush the enemy; the bandits shot at them but could not stop them; he therefore broke them greatly, beheaded heads in excess of a thousand, and captured men and women numbering twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: At the drum the soldiers charged the enemy without hesitation; though the raiders shot at them, they could not be stopped. Gui won a great victory, took more than a thousand heads, and captured twenty thousand men and women.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，授太子詹事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude he was appointed steward of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In 618 he was appointed steward of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 會赤排羌作亂，與薛舉叛將鐘俱仇同寇漢中。

translations.literal: It happened that the Red-Plank Qiang rebelled, and together with Xue Ju's defecting general Zhong Juchou they jointly raided Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When the Red-Plank Qiang rebelled, they joined with Zhong Juchou, a defector from Xue Ju's forces, to raid Hanzhong together.

sentences.zh: 拜軌秦州總管，與賊連戰皆捷，餘黨悉降。

translations.literal: Gui was appointed regional inspector of Qinzhou; in successive battles with the bandits he was always victorious, and the remaining factions all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was appointed regional inspector of Qinzhou; he won every battle against the rebels, and the remaining factions all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 進封酂國公。

translations.literal: He was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Zan.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised in rank to Duke of Zan.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷益州道行台左僕射，許以便宜從事。

translations.literal: In the third year he was moved to left vice director of the Yizhou route grand march secretariat, permitted to act as expedient required.
translations.idiomatic: In 620 he was appointed left vice director of the Yizhou route grand march secretariat with authority to act at his own discretion.

sentences.zh: 屬党項寇松州，詔軌援之，又令扶州刺史蔣善合與軌連勢。

translations.literal: It happened that the Tangut raided Songzhou; an edict ordered Gui to reinforce it, and also ordered Fuzhou prefect Jiang Shanhe to join forces with Gui.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tangut raided Songzhou, Gui was ordered to reinforce the district, and Fuzhou prefect Jiang Shanhe was told to coordinate with him.

sentences.zh: 時党項引吐谷渾之眾，其鋒甚銳。

translations.literal: At that time the Tangut drew the forces of Tuyuhun; their edge was very sharp.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut had drawn in forces from Tuyuhun, and their attack was fierce.

sentences.zh: 軌師未至，善合先期至鉗川，遇賊力戰，走之。

translations.literal: Gui's army had not yet arrived when Shanhe beforehand reached Qianchuan, met the bandits in fierce battle, and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Before Gui's army arrived, Shanhe reached Qianchuan ahead of him, fought the enemy fiercely, and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 軌復軍於臨洮，進擊左封，破其部眾。

translations.literal: Gui regrouped the army at Lintao, advanced to attack Zuofeng, and broke their tribal forces.
translations.idiomatic: Gui regrouped at Lintao, advanced against Zuofeng, and defeated the enemy forces.

sentences.zh: 尋令率所部兵從太宗討王世充於洛陽。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to lead his troops in following Taizong to campaign against Wang Shichong at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was ordered to lead his troops with Taizong in the campaign against Wang Shichong at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 四年，還益州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he returned to Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 621 he returned to Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 時蜀土寇往往聚結，悉討平之。

translations.literal: At that time bandits in Shu territory often gathered in groups; he campaigned and pacified them all.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits in Shu were then gathering in many places, and he suppressed them all.

sentences.zh: 軌每臨戎對寇，或經旬月，身不解甲。

translations.literal: Whenever Gui faced the enemy in battle, sometimes for ten days or a month he did not remove his armor.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Gui went to war he sometimes kept his armor on for ten days or a month at a stretch.

sentences.zh: 其部眾無貴賤少長，不恭命即立斬之。

translations.literal: Among his troops, without regard to noble or base, young or old, whoever did not respect orders was immediately beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Among his troops, whether noble or common, young or old, anyone who disobeyed an order was beheaded on the spot.

sentences.zh: 每日吏士多被鞭撻，流血滿庭，見者莫不重足股慄。

translations.literal: Daily many clerks and soldiers were flogged; blood filled the courtyard, and those who saw it all stood with doubled feet and trembling thighs.
translations.idiomatic: Every day many of his officers and men were flogged until blood filled the courtyard; those who witnessed it trembled with fear.

sentences.zh: 軌初入蜀，將其甥以為心腹，嘗夜出，呼之不以時至，怒而斬之。

translations.literal: When Gui first entered Shu he made his nephew his trusted confidant; once at night he went out and called him, but because he did not arrive in time, in anger he beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gui first entered Shu he made his nephew his trusted confidant; once, when he called for him at night and the nephew failed to come promptly, Gui beheaded him in a rage.

sentences.zh: 每誡家僮不得出外。

translations.literal: He constantly admonished household slaves that they must not go outside.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly forbade his household servants to go outside.

sentences.zh: 嘗遣奴就官廚取漿而悔之，謂奴曰：「我誠使汝，要當斬汝頭以明法耳！」

translations.literal: Once he sent a slave to the official kitchen to fetch gruel and then regretted it, saying to the slave: "I truly sent you, but I must behead your head to clarify the law!"
translations.idiomatic: Once he sent a slave to the official kitchen for gruel, then regretted it and told the slave, "I did send you, but I must cut off your head to uphold the law!"

sentences.zh: 遣其部將收奴斬之。

translations.literal: He sent his subordinate general to seize the slave and behead him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a subordinate officer to seize the slave and behead him.

sentences.zh: 其奴稱冤，監刑者猶豫未決，軌怒，俱斬之。

translations.literal: The slave cried that he was wronged; the overseer of execution hesitated and did not decide; Gui was angry and beheaded them both.
translations.idiomatic: The slave protested his innocence, and the executioner hesitated; Gui in anger had them both beheaded.

sentences.zh: 行台郎中趙弘安，知名士也，軌動輒榜箠，歲至數百。

translations.literal: Grand march secretariat director Zhao Hong'an was a well-known gentleman; Gui whenever he moved would cane and flog him, reaching several hundred times a year.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Hong'an, a director on the grand march staff and a man of reputation, was flogged by Gui on the slightest pretext hundreds of times a year.

sentences.zh: 後徵入朝，賜坐御榻，軌容儀不肅，又坐而對詔，高祖大怒，因謂曰：「公之入蜀，車騎、驃騎從者二十人，為公所斬略盡，我隴種車騎，未足給公。」

translations.literal: Later he was summoned to court and granted a seat on the imperial couch; Gui's bearing was not reverent, and he also sat while responding to the edict; Gaozu was greatly angry and therefore said: "When you entered Shu, twenty attendants of chariots-and-cavalry and swift-cavalry were nearly all beheaded by you—my Longzhong chariots-and-cavalry are not enough to supply you."
translations.idiomatic: Later he was summoned to court and granted a seat on the imperial couch, but Gui's bearing was disrespectful and he remained seated while answering the edict. Gaozu was furious and said, "When you entered Shu you nearly beheaded all twenty of your chariot-and-cavalry attendants. My Longzhong chariot troops are not enough to keep you supplied."

sentences.zh: 詔下獄，俄而釋之，還鎮益州。

translations.literal: An edict sent him to prison; soon he was released and returned to garrison Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent him to prison, but he was soon released and sent back to garrison Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 軌與行台尚書韋雲起、郭行方素不協。

translations.literal: Gui with grand march secretariat director Wei Yunqi and Guo Xingfang had long been incompatible.
translations.idiomatic: Gui had long been on bad terms with grand march directors Wei Yunqi and Guo Xingfang.

sentences.zh: 及隱太子誅，有詔下益州，軌藏諸懷中，雲起問曰：「詔書安在？」

translations.literal: When the Hidden Crown Prince was executed there was an edict sent down to Yizhou; Gui hid it in his bosom; Yunqi asked: "Where is the edict?"
translations.idiomatic: When the Hidden Crown Prince was killed, an edict was sent to Yizhou; Gui hid it in his robe. Yunqi asked, "Where is the edict?"

sentences.zh: 軌不之示，但曰：「卿欲反矣！」

translations.literal: Gui did not show it to him but only said: "You wish to rebel!"
translations.idiomatic: Gui would not show it but said only, "You mean to rebel!"

sentences.zh: 執而殺之。

translations.literal: He seized and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Yunqi and killed him.

sentences.zh: 行方大懼，奔於京師，軌追斬不及。

translations.literal: Xingfang was greatly afraid and fled to the capital; Gui pursued but could not catch and behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Xingfang fled in terror to the capital; Gui pursued him but could not overtake and kill him.

sentences.zh: 是歲，行台廢，即授益州大都督，加食邑六百戶。

translations.literal: That year the grand march secretariat was abolished; he was at once appointed great regional inspector of Yizhou with an added fief of six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: That year the grand march secretariat was abolished; he was appointed great regional inspector of Yizhou with an added fief of six hundred households.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，征授右衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan he was summoned and appointed general of the right guard.
translations.idiomatic: In 627 he was summoned and appointed general of the right guard.

sentences.zh: 二年，出為洛州都督。

translations.literal: In the second year he went out as regional inspector of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 628 he was sent out as regional inspector of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 洛陽因隋末喪亂，人多浮偽。

translations.literal: Because of the disorders and chaos at the end of Sui, the people of Luoyang were largely shiftless and false.
translations.idiomatic: Because of the chaos at the end of the Sui, the people of Luoyang had grown shiftless and deceitful.

sentences.zh: 軌並遣務農，各令屬縣有游手怠惰者皆按之。

translations.literal: Gui together sent agricultural commissioners and ordered each subordinate county to investigate all idlers and the lazy.
translations.idiomatic: Gui sent out agricultural commissioners and ordered every subordinate county to prosecute idlers and the indolent.

sentences.zh: 由是人吏懾憚，風化整肅。

translations.literal: Thereby officials and people were in fearful awe and customs were put in good order.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners alike were awed into obedience, and local customs were restored to good order.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒官，贈并州都督。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died in office and was posthumously made regional inspector of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 621 he died in office and was posthumously appointed regional inspector of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 子奉節嗣，尚高祖永嘉公主，歷左衛將軍、秦州都督。

translations.literal: His son Fengjie succeeded him, married Princess Yongjia of Gaozu, and successively served as general of the Left Guard and regional inspector of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fengjie succeeded him, married Gaozu's daughter Princess Yongjia, and rose to general of the Left Guard and regional inspector of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 窦琮軌弟琮，亦有武干，隋左親衛。

translations.literal: Dou Cong, Gui's younger brother Cong, also had martial capacity and in Sui served in the Left Personal Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Cong, Gui's younger brother, also showed military talent and had served in the Sui Left Personal Guard.

sentences.zh: 大業末，犯法，亡命奔太原，依於高祖。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye he violated the law, fled as a fugitive to Taiyuan, and attached himself to Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Daye era he broke the law, fled to Taiyuan, and placed himself under Gaozu's protection.

sentences.zh: 琮與太宗有宿憾，每自疑。

translations.literal: Cong and Taizong had an old grievance, and he constantly doubted himself.
translations.idiomatic: Cong and the future Taizong had an old grudge, and he was always uneasy in his presence.

sentences.zh: 太宗方蒐羅英傑，降禮納之，出入臥內，其意乃解。

translations.literal: Taizong was then gathering outstanding men, lowered ritual to receive him, and had him enter and leave the inner quarters; his mind was then relieved.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was then recruiting talented men, received him with lowered ceremony, and admitted him to his private quarters until his suspicions eased.

sentences.zh: 及將義舉，琮協贊大謀。

translations.literal: When the righteous uprising was about to be raised, Cong cooperated in supporting the great plan.
translations.idiomatic: When the uprising was being planned, Cong helped shape the grand strategy.

sentences.zh: 大將軍府建，為統軍。

translations.literal: When the great general's headquarters was established, he was made army commander.
translations.idiomatic: When the great general's headquarters was established, he was appointed an army commander.

sentences.zh: 從平西河，破霍邑，拜金紫光祿大夫、扶風郡公。

translations.literal: Following in the pacification of Xihe and the defeat at Huoyi, he was made Grand Master of Splendor and Virtue with the Golden Seal and Duke of Fufeng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the pacification of Xihe and the victory at Huoyi, and was appointed Grand Master of Splendor and Virtue with the Golden Seal and Duke of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 尋從劉文靜擊屈突通於潼關，通遣裨將桑顯和來逼文靜，義軍不利。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he followed Liu Wenjing in attacking Qu Tuotong at Tong Pass; Qu sent his subordinate general Sang Xianhe to press Wenjing, and the righteous army fared badly.
translations.idiomatic: He soon joined Liu Wenjing in attacking Qu Tuotong at Tong Pass; Qu sent his lieutenant Sang Xianhe to press Wenjing's force, and the rebel army began to falter.

sentences.zh: 琮與段志玄等力戰久之，隋軍大潰，通遁走。

translations.literal: Cong with Duan Zhixuan and others fought fiercely for a long time; the Sui army was greatly routed and Qu fled.
translations.idiomatic: Cong, Duan Zhixuan, and others fought hard for a long time until the Sui army broke and Qu Tuotong fled.

sentences.zh: 琮率輕騎追至稠桑，獲通而返。

translations.literal: Cong led light cavalry in pursuit to Chousang, captured Qu, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Cong led light cavalry in pursuit to Chousang, captured Qu Tuotong, and returned in triumph.

sentences.zh: 進兵東略，下陝縣，拔太原倉。

translations.literal: Advancing eastward he reduced Shan county and seized Taiyuan granary.
translations.idiomatic: He marched east, took Shan county, and captured the Taiyuan granary.

sentences.zh: 拜右領軍大將軍，賜物五百段。

translations.literal: He was appointed great general of the Right Army Guard and bestowed five hundred bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: He was made great general of the Right Army Guard and rewarded with five hundred bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 時隋河陽都尉獨孤武潛謀歸國，乃令琮以步騎一萬自柏崖道應接之。

translations.literal: At that time the Sui commandant of Heyang, Dugu Wu, secretly plotted to return to the cause, so Cong was ordered to take ten thousand infantry and cavalry by the Baiya route to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sui commandant of Heyang, Dugu Wu, secretly planned to defect, Cong was ordered to take ten thousand foot and horse soldiers by the Baiya route to link up with him.

sentences.zh: 遲留不進，武見殺，坐是除名。

translations.literal: He delayed and did not advance; Wu was killed, and for this he was stripped of rank.
translations.idiomatic: He lingered and failed to advance; Dugu Wu was killed, and Cong was dismissed from office for it.

sentences.zh: 武德初，以元謀勳特恕一死，拜右屯衛大將軍，復轉右領軍大將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude, because of his original planning merit he was specially pardoned one death sentence, appointed great general of the Right Garrison Guard, and again transferred to great general of the Right Army Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wude era his founding service won him a special reprieve from the death penalty; he was appointed great general of the Right Garrison Guard and later restored as great general of the Right Army Guard.

sentences.zh: 時將圖洛陽，遣琮留守陝城，以督糧運。

translations.literal: When they were about to target Luoyang, Cong was sent to remain and hold Shancheng to supervise grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: As the court prepared to move on Luoyang, Cong was left at Shancheng to oversee the grain supply.

sentences.zh: 王世充遣其驍將羅士信來斷糧道，琮潛使人說以利害，士信遂帥眾降。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong sent his fierce general Luo Shixin to cut the grain route; Cong secretly sent men to persuade him of advantage and harm, and Shixin thereupon led his followers in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong sent his fierce general Luo Shixin to sever the supply line; Cong secretly sent envoys to argue the costs and benefits, and Shixin surrendered with his troops.

sentences.zh: 及從平東都，賞物一千四百段。

translations.literal: When he followed in the pacification of the Eastern Capital, he was rewarded with one thousand four hundred bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: After he took part in the pacification of the Eastern Capital, he was rewarded with fourteen hundred bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 後以本官檢校晉州總管。

translations.literal: Later, while retaining his original office, he was made acting regional commander of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed acting regional commander of Jinzhou while retaining his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 尋從隱太子討平劉黑闥，以功封譙國公，賞黃金五十斤。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he followed the Hidden Crown Prince in suppressing Liu Heita; for merit he was enfeoffed as Duke of Qiao and rewarded with fifty jin of gold.
translations.idiomatic: He soon joined the Hidden Crown Prince in putting down Liu Heita, was enfeoffed as Duke of Qiao for his service, and rewarded with fifty jin of gold.

sentences.zh: 未幾而卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 高祖以佐命之舊，甚悼之，贈左衛大將軍，謚曰敬。

translations.literal: Gaozu, because of his old service in founding the mandate, deeply mourned him, posthumously made him great general of the Left Guard, and gave him the posthumous title Respectful.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu mourned him deeply as an old companion in founding the dynasty, posthumously appointed him great general of the Left Guard, and gave him the posthumous title Respectful.

sentences.zh: 永徽五年，重贈特進。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yonghui he was again posthumously made Special Advancement.
translations.idiomatic: In 654 he was posthumously promoted again to Special Advancement.

sentences.zh: 窦抗抗，字道生，太穆皇后之從兄也，隋洛州總管、陳國公榮之子也。

translations.literal: Dou Kang. Kang, styled Daosheng, was a cousin of Empress Taimu and son of Rong, Sui regional commander of Luozhou and Duke of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Kang. Kang, styled Daosheng, was a cousin of Empress Taimu and the son of Rong, Sui regional commander of Luozhou and Duke of Chen.

sentences.zh: 母，隋文帝萬安公主。

translations.literal: His mother was Princess Wan'an, daughter of Emperor Wen of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Emperor Wen of Sui's daughter, Princess Wan'an.

sentences.zh: 抗在隋以帝甥甚見崇寵。

translations.literal: Kang in Sui, as the emperor's sister's son, was greatly honored and favored.
translations.idiomatic: In the Sui, as the emperor's nephew by marriage, Kang enjoyed exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 少入太學，略涉書史，釋褐千牛備身、儀同三司。

translations.literal: In youth he entered the Imperial Academy, lightly touched books and history, and upon first taking office became attendant of the Thousand-Ox Guard and honorary third-rank official.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied at the Imperial Academy and gained a modest grounding in the classics and history; on entering service he became an attendant of the Thousand-Ox Guard with honorary third-rank status.

sentences.zh: 屬其父寢疾，抗躬親扶侍，衣不解帶者五十餘日。

translations.literal: When his father took to bed ill, Kang personally attended and supported him, not loosening his belt for more than fifty days.
translations.idiomatic: When his father fell gravely ill, Kang nursed him in person and did not change his clothes for more than fifty days.

sentences.zh: 及居喪，哀毀過禮。

translations.literal: When he entered mourning, his grief and emaciation exceeded ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning he grieved so deeply that his grief exceeded what ritual prescribed.

sentences.zh: 後襲爵陳國公，累轉梁州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he inherited the title Duke of Chen and successively transferred to regional inspector of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later inherited the title Duke of Chen and rose to regional inspector of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 將之官，隋文帝幸其第，命抗及公主酣宴，如家人之禮，賞賜極厚。

translations.literal: When he was about to go to his post, Emperor Wen of Sui visited his residence, ordered Kang and the princess to feast freely with the rites of family members, and bestowed rewards of extreme generosity.
translations.idiomatic: Before he took up his post, Emperor Wen visited his home, had Kang and the princess dine with him as family, and lavished gifts upon them.

sentences.zh: 母卒，號慟絕而復甦者數焉，文帝令宮人至第，節其哭泣。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he wailed until he collapsed and revived several times; Emperor Wen sent palace women to his residence to moderate his weeping.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he wailed until he fainted several times; Emperor Wen sent palace women to his home to restrain his grief.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，起為岐州刺史，轉幽州總管，政並以寬惠聞。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was recalled and made regional inspector of Qizhou, then transferred to regional commander of Youzhou; in both posts his governance was known for leniency and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he returned to office as regional inspector of Qizhou, then became regional commander of Youzhou; in both posts he was known for lenient and benevolent rule.

sentences.zh: 及漢王諒作亂，煬帝恐其為變，遣李子雄馳往代之。

translations.literal: When Prince Han Liang rebelled, Emperor Yang feared Kang might change sides and sent Li Zixiong posthaste to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Han Liang rebelled, Emperor Yang feared Kang might turn against the throne and sent Li Zixiong posthaste to replace him.

sentences.zh: 子雄因言抗得諒書而不奏，按之無驗，以疑貳除名。

translations.literal: Zixiong thereupon said Kang had received a letter from Liang but had not reported it; investigation found no proof, yet on suspicion of divided loyalty he was stripped of rank.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zixiong claimed Kang had received a letter from Liang but failed to report it; though the charge could not be verified, he was dismissed on suspicion of disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 抗與高祖少相親狎，及楊玄感作亂，高祖統兵隴右，抗言於高祖曰：「玄感抑為發蹤耳！

translations.literal: Kang and Gaozu had been close since youth; when Yang Xuangan rebelled and Gaozu commanded troops in Longyou, Kang spoke to Gaozu, saying: "Xuangan is at most the one who looses the hounds!
translations.idiomatic: Kang had been close to Gaozu since youth; when Yang Xuangan rebelled and Gaozu commanded troops in Longyou, Kang told him, "Xuangan is only the man who sets the hounds running!

sentences.zh: 李氏有名圖籙，可乘其便，天之所啟也。」

translations.literal: The Li clan has a name in charts and registers; one may seize the opportunity—it is what Heaven has opened."
translations.idiomatic: The Li house has a place in the prophecy books; we can seize the moment—Heaven itself is opening the way."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「無為禍始，何言之妄也！」

translations.literal: Gaozu said: "Do not be the origin of calamity—how wildly you speak!"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu replied, "Do not be the author of disaster—how reckless your words are!"

sentences.zh: 大業末，抗於靈武巡長城以伺盜賊，及聞高祖定京城，抗對眾而忭曰：「此吾家妹婿也，豁達有大度，真撥亂之主矣！」

translations.literal: At the end of Daye, Kang at Lingwu patrolled the Great Wall to watch for bandits; when he heard Gaozu had secured the capital, Kang said joyfully before the assembly: "This is my family's son-in-law—openhanded and of great magnanimity, truly a lord who will put chaos in order!"
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Daye era Kang was at Lingwu patrolling the Great Wall against bandits; when he heard Gaozu had taken the capital, he exclaimed before the crowd, "That is my family's son-in-law—magnanimous and far-sighted, truly a ruler who can restore order from chaos!"

sentences.zh: 因歸長安。

translations.literal: Thereupon he returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 高祖見之大悅，握手引坐曰：「李氏竟能成事，何如？」

translations.literal: Gaozu was greatly pleased on seeing him, grasped his hand and drew him to sit, saying: "Can the Li clan actually accomplish the enterprise—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was delighted to see him, took his hand, and drew him to sit, saying, "So the Li house can actually succeed—what do you think?"

sentences.zh: 因縱酒為樂。

translations.literal: Thereupon they drank freely for pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Then they drank freely in celebration.

sentences.zh: 尋拜將作大匠。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed chief artisan of palace construction.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed chief artisan of palace construction.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，以本官兼納言。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude he was additionally made chief censor while retaining his original office.
translations.idiomatic: In 618 he was additionally appointed chief censor while retaining his existing post.

sentences.zh: 高祖聽朝，或升御坐，退朝之後，延入臥內，命之舍敬，縱酒談謔，敦平生之款。

translations.literal: When Gaozu held court, Kang sometimes ascended the imperial seat; after court was dismissed he was invited into the inner quarters, ordered to set aside formality, drank freely and joked, and deepened the warmth of their lifelong friendship.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu held court Kang sometimes sat beside him on the imperial seat; after court he was invited into the private quarters, told to put aside ceremony, and they drank and bantered as old friends.

sentences.zh: 常侍宴移時，或留宿禁內。

translations.literal: He often attended banquets for long stretches, and sometimes stayed overnight within the forbidden precinct.
translations.idiomatic: He often kept Gaozu company at feasts for hours and sometimes spent the night inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 高祖每呼為兄而不名也，宮內咸稱為舅。
