translations.literal: Gaozu always addressed him as Elder Brother without using his name, and within the palace all called him Uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu always called him Elder Brother rather than by name, and everyone in the palace referred to him as Uncle.

sentences.zh: 常陪侍游宴，不知朝務。

translations.literal: He constantly accompanied Gaozu in outings and banquets and knew nothing of court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He spent his time at Gaozu's side in outings and banquets and took no part in state business.

sentences.zh: 轉左武候大將軍，領左右千牛備身大將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to great general of the Left Martial Guard and concurrently great general commanding the Left and Right Thousand-Ox Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: He became great general of the Left Martial Guard and also commanded the Left and Right Thousand-Ox Attendants.

sentences.zh: 尋從太宗平薛舉，勳居第一。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he followed Taizong in pacifying Xue Ju, and his merit ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: He soon joined Taizong in defeating Xue Ju and ranked first in merit.

sentences.zh: 四年，又從征王世充。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he again followed in the campaign against Wang Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: In 621 he again took part in the campaign against Wang Shichong.

sentences.zh: 及東都平，冊勳太廟者九人，抗與從弟軌俱預焉。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Capital was pacified, nine men were enregistered for merit in the Imperial Ancestral Temple; Kang and his younger cousin Gui were both included.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Capital fell, nine men were enshrined for merit in the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and both Kang and his cousin Gui were among them.

sentences.zh: 朝廷榮之，賜女樂一部、金寶萬計。

translations.literal: The court honored them and bestowed a troupe of female musicians and gold and jewels numbering in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The court honored them with a troupe of female musicians and treasures beyond count.

sentences.zh: 武德四年，因侍宴暴卒，贈司空，謚曰密。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude he suddenly died while attending a banquet; he was posthumously made Minister of Works and given the posthumous title Scrupulous.
translations.idiomatic: In 621 he died suddenly at a banquet; he was posthumously appointed Minister of Works and given the posthumous title Scrupulous.

sentences.zh: 子衍。

translations.literal: His son Yan.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yan.

sentences.zh: 衍嗣，官至左武衛將軍。

translations.literal: Yan succeeded him and reached the post of general of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yan succeeded him and rose to general of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 時抗群從內三品七人，四品、五品十餘人，尚主三人，妃數人，冠冕之盛，當朝無比。

translations.literal: At that time among Kang's clan cousins there were seven of third rank within the palace, more than ten of fourth and fifth rank, three who married princesses, and several who became consorts—the splendor of caps and sashes was unmatched in the court.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Kang's clan included seven third-rank officials inside the palace, more than ten of fourth and fifth rank, three princess consorts, and several imperial consorts—no family at court matched their rank and honors.

sentences.zh: 窦靜靜，字元休，抗第二子也。

translations.literal: Dou Jing. Jing, styled Yuanxiu, was Kang's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jing. Jing, styled Yuanxiu, was Kang's second son.

sentences.zh: 武德初，累轉并州大總管府長史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude he successively transferred to chief administrator of the great regional headquarters of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wude era he rose to chief administrator of the great regional headquarters at Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 時突厥數為邊患，師旅歲興，軍糧不屬，靜表請太原置屯田以省饋運。

translations.literal: At that time the Turks repeatedly became a border affliction, armies were raised every year, and military grain did not suffice; Jing submitted a memorial requesting garrison farms be established at Taiyuan to reduce supply transport.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks were raiding the frontier repeatedly, campaigns were mounted every year, and grain supplies could not keep up; Jing memorialized the throne to establish garrison farms at Taiyuan and cut supply costs.

sentences.zh: 時議者以民物凋零，不宜動眾，書奏不省。

translations.literal: Opinion at the time held that the people and goods were withered and it was unsuitable to mobilize the masses; the memorial was not examined.
translations.idiomatic: Critics argued that the people and economy were too depleted for such an effort, and the memorial went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 靜頻上書，辭甚切至。

translations.literal: Jing repeatedly submitted memorials, his language extremely urgent and direct.
translations.idiomatic: Jing submitted memorial after memorial in urgent and forceful language.

sentences.zh: 於是征靜入朝，與裴寂、蕭瑀、封德彝等爭論於殿庭，寂等不能屈，竟從靜議。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jing was summoned to court and debated in the hall with Pei Ji, Xiao Yu, Feng Deyi, and others; Ji and the others could not refute him, and in the end his proposal was followed.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was then summoned to court and debated the matter in the hall with Pei Ji, Xiao Yu, Feng Deyi, and others; they could not defeat his argument, and the court adopted his plan.

sentences.zh: 歲收數千斛，高祖善之，令檢校并州大總管。

translations.literal: The yearly harvest reached several thousand hu; Gaozu approved it and made him acting great regional commander of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The farms yielded several thousand hu each year; Gaozu approved and appointed him acting great regional commander of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 靜又以突厥頻來入寇，請斷石嶺以為障塞，復從之。

translations.literal: Jing also, because the Turks repeatedly came in raiding, requested that Shiling be cut off to serve as a barrier, and this too was followed.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Turks kept raiding across the border, Jing also proposed blocking Shiling Pass as a defensive barrier, and that plan too was adopted.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，征拜司農卿，封信都男，尋轉夏州都督。

translations.literal: When Taizong acceded, Jing was summoned and appointed minister of agriculture, enfeoffed as Baron of Xindu, and soon transferred to regional inspector of Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong came to the throne, Jing was summoned and appointed minister of agriculture, enfeoffed as Baron of Xindu, and soon made regional inspector of Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 值突厥攜貳，諸將出征，多詣其所。

translations.literal: It happened that the Turks were divided in loyalty; when generals went on campaign many came to his place.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks split into rival factions, many commanders bound for the frontier came to consult him.

sentences.zh: 靜知虜中虛實，潛令人間其部落，郁射設所部郁孤尼等九俟斤並率眾歸款，太宗稱善，賜馬百匹、羊千口。

translations.literal: Jing knew the true and false within the barbarians and secretly sent men to sow division among their tribes; the nine yabgu under Yugu Ni and others in the division of Yushshe all led their followers in submission, Taizong praised him, and bestowed one hundred horses and one thousand sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the Turks' strengths and weaknesses, Jing secretly sent agents to divide their tribes; nine yabgu under Yugu Ni and others in Yushshe's division surrendered with their followers, and Taizong rewarded him with a hundred horses and a thousand sheep.

sentences.zh: 及擒頡利，處其部眾於河南，以為不便，上封曰：「臣聞夷狄者，同夫禽獸，窮則搏噬，群則聚塵。

translations.literal: When Jieli was captured and his tribes were settled south of the Yellow River, Jing deemed it inadvisable and submitted a sealed memorial, saying: "Your subject has heard that the barbarians are like beasts—when cornered they bite and claw, when massed they raise dust.
translations.idiomatic: After Jieli was captured and his tribes were resettled south of the Yellow River, Jing thought the policy unwise and submitted a sealed memorial: "Your subject has heard that barbarians are like beasts—cornered, they turn and attack; massed together, they stir up dust.

sentences.zh: 不可以刑法威，不可以仁義教。

translations.literal: They cannot be awed by penal law, and cannot be taught by benevolence and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: They cannot be controlled by penal law, nor reformed by benevolence and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 衣食仰給，不務耕桑，徒損有為之民，以資無知之虜，得之則無益於治，失之則無損於化。

translations.literal: Food and clothing rely on others' supply; they do not engage in farming and sericulture, vainly harming productive subjects to support ignorant barbarians—gaining them brings no benefit to good order, losing them brings no harm to transformation.
translations.idiomatic: They live on handouts rather than farming or weaving, wasting productive subjects to sustain ignorant barbarians; keeping them brings no benefit to good government, and losing them would not harm civilization.

sentences.zh: 然彼首丘之情，未易忘也，誠恐一旦變生，犯我王略，愚臣之所深慮。

translations.literal: Yet their feeling of attachment to the old mound is not easily forgotten; I truly fear that if change arises in a single day they will violate our royal domain—this is what your foolish subject deeply worries about.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they will not easily forget their old homelands; I truly fear that one day they will rebel and violate our territory—this is what deeply troubles your foolish subject.

sentences.zh: 如臣計者，莫如因其破亡之後，加其無妄之福，假以賢王之號，妻以宗室之女，分其土地，析其部落，使其權弱勢分，易為羈制。

translations.literal: As your subject calculates it, nothing is better than after their destruction and defeat to add undeserved favor, lend them the title of worthy prince, marry them to daughters of the imperial clan, divide their lands, and split their tribes, causing their power to be weak and strength divided—thus easy to control by restraint.
translations.idiomatic: In my view, once they are broken and defeated we should grant them unearned favor, invest them with princely titles, marry them to imperial clanswomen, divide their lands, and split their tribes until their power is weakened and fragmented and they are easy to control.

sentences.zh: 自可永保邊塞，俾為籓臣，此實長轡遠馭之道。」

translations.literal: Then the border can forever be secured and they made vassal ministers—this is truly the way of holding long reins to drive from afar."
translations.idiomatic: That way the frontier can be secured for good and they can be kept as vassal subjects—this is truly the art of ruling distant peoples from afar."

sentences.zh: 於時務在懷輯，雖未從之，太宗深嘉其志。

translations.literal: At that time the policy lay in conciliation; though they did not follow his plan, Taizong deeply approved his intention.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court prioritized conciliation; though his plan was not adopted, Taizong greatly admired his purpose.

sentences.zh: 制曰：「北方之務，悉以相委，以卿為寧朔大使，撫鎮華戎，朕無北顧之憂矣。」

translations.literal: An edict said: "Northern affairs shall all be entrusted to you; I appoint you Pacifier of the North envoy to soothe and govern Chinese and barbarians—I have no more worry about looking north."
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "All northern affairs are entrusted to you; I appoint you Pacifier of the North to govern both Chinese and barbarians, and I need no longer worry about the northern frontier."

sentences.zh: 再遷民部尚書。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to minister of the household.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to minister of the household.

sentences.zh: 貞觀九年卒，謚曰肅。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhenguan he died and was given the posthumous title Solemn.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 635 and was given the posthumous title Solemn.

sentences.zh: 子逵。

translations.literal: His son Kui.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Kui.

sentences.zh: 逵尚太宗女遂安公主，襲爵信都男。

translations.literal: Kui married Taizong's daughter Princess Sui'an and inherited the title Baron of Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: Kui married Taizong's daughter Princess Sui'an and inherited the title Baron of Xindu.

sentences.zh: 窦誕誕，抗第三子也。

translations.literal: Dou Dan. Dan was Kang's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Dan. Dan was Kang's third son.

sentences.zh: 隋仁壽中，起家為朝請郎。

translations.literal: In the Renshou era of Sui he first entered office as court gentleman for palace attendance.
translations.idiomatic: During the Renshou era he began his career as a court gentleman for palace attendance.

sentences.zh: 義寧初，辟丞相府祭酒，轉殿中監，封安豐郡公，尚高祖女襄陽公主。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yining he was recruited as libationer of the chancellor's headquarters, transferred to director of the palace bureau, enfeoffed as Duke of Anfeng commandery, and married Gaozu's daughter Princess Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yining era he was appointed libationer on the chancellor's staff, then director of the palace bureau, enfeoffed as Duke of Anfeng, and married Gaozu's daughter Princess Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 從太宗征薛舉，為元帥府司馬。

translations.literal: Following Taizong in the campaign against Xue Ju, he served as marshal of the commander-in-chief's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Taizong's campaign against Xue Ju as marshal on the commander's staff.

sentences.zh: 遷刑部尚書，轉太常卿。

translations.literal: He was moved to minister of justice and transferred to minister of imperial rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed minister of justice and then minister of imperial rites.

sentences.zh: 高祖諸少子荊王元景等未出宮者十餘王，所有國司家產之事，皆令誕主之。

translations.literal: Among Gaozu's younger sons, more than ten princes including Prince Jing Yuanjing who had not yet left the palace—all matters of fief administration and household property were ordered to be managed by Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu put Dan in charge of fief administration and household affairs for more than ten younger princes who had not yet left the palace, including Prince Jing Yuanjing.

sentences.zh: 出為梁州都督。

translations.literal: He went out as regional inspector of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as regional inspector of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，召拜右領軍大將軍，轉大理卿、莘國公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was summoned and appointed great general of the Right Army Guard, then transferred to chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review and Duke of Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan era he was recalled as great general of the Right Army Guard, then appointed chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review and Duke of Shen.

sentences.zh: 修營太廟，賜物五百段。

translations.literal: For repairing and constructing the Imperial Ancestral Temple he was bestowed five hundred bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: For overseeing repairs to the Imperial Ancestral Temple he was rewarded with five hundred bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 復為殿中監，以疾解官，復拜宗正卿。

translations.literal: He again became director of the palace bureau, resigned on account of illness, and was again appointed minister of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as director of the palace bureau, resigned because of illness, and was later reappointed minister of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 太宗常與之言，昏忘不能對，乃手詔曰：「朕聞為官擇人者治，為人擇官者亂。

translations.literal: Taizong often spoke with him, but befuddled by forgetfulness he could not reply; Taizong then wrote a hand edict, saying: "I have heard that he who selects men for office governs well, he who selects offices for men brings disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong often spoke with him, but Dan, confused and forgetful, could not answer; Taizong then issued a personal edict: "I have heard that choosing the right men for office brings order, while choosing offices for the wrong men brings chaos.

sentences.zh: 竇誕比來精神衰耗，殊異常時。

translations.literal: Dou Dan of late has been mentally exhausted and decayed, greatly unlike his former self.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Dan's mind has lately failed him, and he is nothing like the man he once was.

sentences.zh: 知不肖而任之，睹尸祿而不退，非唯傷風亂政，亦恐為君不明。

translations.literal: Knowing him unworthy yet appointing him, seeing he occupies salary yet does not withdraw—not only does this harm customs and disorder government, I also fear it shows the ruler unclear.
translations.idiomatic: To know a man is unfit yet keep him in office, to see him draw salary without serving—not only corrupts public morals and disrupts government, it also makes the ruler look unwise.

sentences.zh: 考績黜陟，古今常典，誕可光祿大夫還第。」

translations.literal: Examination of merit for promotion and dismissal is the constant norm of ancients and moderns—Dan may become Supernumerary Palace Counselor and return home."
translations.idiomatic: Merit reviews and dismissals are the rule in every age; Dan is hereby made Supernumerary Palace Counselor and sent home."

sentences.zh: 尋卒，贈工部尚書、荊州刺史，謚曰安。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died; he was posthumously made minister of public works and prefect of Jingzhou, and given the posthumous title Tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward and was posthumously appointed minister of public works and prefect of Jingzhou, with the posthumous title Tranquil.

sentences.zh: 子孝慈。

translations.literal: His son Xiaoci.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Xiaoci.

sentences.zh: 孝慈嗣，官至左衛將軍。

translations.literal: Xiaoci succeeded him and reached the post of general of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoci succeeded him and rose to general of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 孝慈子希玠。

translations.literal: Xiaoci's son Xijie.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoci's son was Xijie.

sentences.zh: 希玠少襲爵，中宗時為禮部尚書，以恩澤賜實封二百五十戶。

translations.literal: Xijie in youth succeeded to the title; in the time of Emperor Zhongzong he was Minister of Rites and by grace was granted a substantive fief of two hundred fifty households.
translations.idiomatic: Xijie succeeded to the title while young; under Emperor Zhongzong he served as Minister of Rites and was granted a substantive fief of two hundred fifty households as a mark of favor.

sentences.zh: 開元初為太子少傅、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan he was made junior tutor of the crown prince and commissioner with the ceremonial parity of the Three Excellencies and an opening office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyuan era he was appointed junior tutor of the crown prince and commissioner with ceremonial parity of the Three Excellencies and an opening office.

sentences.zh: 誕少子孝諶，在《外戚傳》。

translations.literal: Dan's younger son Xiaochen is treated in the 《Biography of Affinal Kin》.
translations.idiomatic: Dan's younger son Xiaochen is treated in the 《Biography of Affinal Kin》.

sentences.zh: 竇氏自武德至今，再為外戚，一品三人，三品已上三十餘人，尚主者八人，女為王妃六人，唐世貴盛，莫與為比。

translations.literal: The Dou clan from Wude to the present twice became affinal kin; three men of first rank, more than thirty of third rank and above, eight who married princesses, six daughters who became princely consorts—in Tang's age of noble flourishing none could be compared.
translations.idiomatic: From the Wude era to the present the Dou clan twice became imperial affines: three men of the highest rank, more than thirty of third rank or above, eight who married princesses, and six daughters who became princely consorts. No family in Tang times matched their eminence.

sentences.zh: 窦璡璡，字之推，抗季弟也。

translations.literal: Dou Jin. Jin, styled Zhitui, was Kang's youngest brother.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jin. Jin, styled Zhitui, was Kang's youngest brother.

sentences.zh: 大業末，為扶風太守。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye he was prefect of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Daye era he served as prefect of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 高祖定京師，以郡歸國，歷禮部、民部二尚書。

translations.literal: When Gaozu secured the capital region, he submitted the commandery to the new state and successively served as Minister of Rites and Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu secured the capital, Jin surrendered his commandery and served in turn as Minister of Rites and Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 從太宗平薛仁杲。

translations.literal: He followed Taizong in pacifying Xue Rengao.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Taizong in the campaign that pacified Xue Rengao.

sentences.zh: 尋鎮益州，時蜀中尚多寇賊，璡屢討平之。

translations.literal: Soon he garrisoned Yizhou; at that time Shu still had many bandits and raiders, and Jin repeatedly campaigned and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was posted to Yizhou; bandits were still numerous in Shu, and Jin repeatedly campaigned until he had suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 時皇甫無逸在蜀，與之不協，璡屢請入朝。

translations.literal: At that time Huangfu Wuyi was in Shu and was incompatible with him; Jin repeatedly requested to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Wuyi was then in Shu and at odds with him; Jin repeatedly asked to return to court.

sentences.zh: 高祖征之，中路詔令還鎮。

translations.literal: Gaozu summoned him, but midway an edict ordered him back to his garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu summoned him, but an edict midway ordered him back to his post.

sentences.zh: 璡不得志，遂於路左題山，以申鬱積。

translations.literal: Jin did not achieve his wish and thereupon inscribed a mountain beside the road to express his pent-up feelings.
translations.idiomatic: Frustrated in his ambitions, he inscribed a cliff beside the road to vent his grievance.

sentences.zh: 有使者至其所，璡宴之臥內，遺以綾綺。

translations.literal: When an envoy came to his place, Jin feasted him in his sleeping quarters and gave him silks and brocades.
translations.idiomatic: When an envoy came to visit him, Jin entertained him in his private quarters and gave him silks and brocades.

sentences.zh: 無逸奏其事，坐免官。

translations.literal: Wuyi memorialized the matter and he was dismissed from office for it.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyi reported the affair to the throne, and Jin was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜秘書監，封鄧國公。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed director of the Secretariat and enfeoffed as Duke of Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed director of the Secretariat and enfeoffed as Duke of Deng.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，授太子詹事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was appointed steward of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan era he was appointed steward of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 後為將作大匠，修葺洛陽宮。

translations.literal: Later he was made master of works and repaired the Luoyang palace.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed master of works and put in charge of repairing the Luoyang palace.

sentences.zh: 璡於宮中鑿池起山，崇飾雕麗，虛費功力，太宗怒，遽令毀之。

translations.literal: Jin within the palace dug pools and raised mountains, with lofty ornament and carved splendor, wasting labor in vain; Taizong was angry and immediately ordered it destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Jin had pools dug and artificial mountains built within the palace, lavishly decorated at great waste of labor; Taizong was furious and ordered everything torn down at once.

sentences.zh: 坐事免。

translations.literal: He was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed because of the affair.

sentences.zh: 會納其女為酆王妃，俄而復位，加右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: It happened that his daughter was taken in as consort of the Prince of Feng; soon he was restored to office and made right grand master for splendid happiness.
translations.idiomatic: When his daughter was married to the Prince of Feng, he was soon restored to office and appointed right grand master for splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 七年卒，贈禮部尚書，謚曰安。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died; posthumously made Minister of Rites; posthumous title Tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 633; he was posthumously appointed Minister of Rites and given the posthumous title Tranquil.

sentences.zh: 璡頗曉音律，武德中，與太常少卿祖孝孫受詔定正聲雅樂，璡討論故實，撰《正聲調》一卷，行於代。

translations.literal: Jin was quite versed in pitch and regulation; in Wude, together with vice director of the Court of Sacrifices Zu Xiaosun he received an edict to fix the correct tones and elegant music; Jin discussed ancient precedents and compiled one fascicle of the 《Correct Tones》, which circulated in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was well versed in music theory; during the Wude era he and Vice Director of the Court of Sacrifices Zu Xiaosun were ordered to establish the correct pitches and court music. Jin researched historical precedents and compiled one fascicle of the 《Correct Tones》, which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：得人者昌，如諸溫儒雅清顯，為一時之稱；

translations.literal: The historiographer says: He who gains men flourishes—as with the various Wen, refined and elegant, clear and eminent, acclaimed in their time;
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer remarks: States flourish when they gain the right men. The Wen brothers, refined and eminent, were acclaimed in their day;

sentences.zh: 叔達才學明辯，中二國之選。

translations.literal: Shuda in talent and learning was clear in argument, chosen among the two states;
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shuda was gifted, learned, and eloquent, chosen from both the Chen and Tang courts;

sentences.zh: 皆抱廊廟之器，俱為社稷之臣。

translations.literal: all embraced the vessels of the hall and temple and alike were ministers of the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: all possessed the capacity for high office and served as pillars of the state.

sentences.zh: 威守道，軌臨戎，抗居喪，靜經略，璡音律，仍以懿親，俱至顯位；

translations.literal: Wei kept the Way, Gui faced battle, Kang dwelt in mourning, Jing in strategy, Jin in pitch and regulation—still further as honored kin, all reached eminent posts;
translations.idiomatic: Wei upheld the Way, Gui took the field, Kang was famed for filial mourning, Jing for frontier strategy, and Jin for music; as imperial kin they too rose to eminent posts;

sentences.zh: 才能門第，輝映數朝，豈非得人歟？

translations.literal: talent and lineage shining across several reigns—is this not indeed gaining men?
translations.idiomatic: their talent and lineage shining across several reigns—was this not proof that Tang had gained the right men?

sentences.zh: 唐之昌也，不亦宜乎！

translations.literal: That Tang flourished—was it not fitting!
translations.idiomatic: Small wonder that Tang flourished as it did!

sentences.zh: 然彥博之褊，竇軌之酷，亦非全器焉。

translations.literal: Yet Yanbo's narrowness and Dou Gui's harshness were also not complete vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yanbo's narrowness and Dou Gui's cruelty show that even these men were not without flaw.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：溫、陳才位，文蔚典禮。

translations.literal: Praise says: Wen and Chen in talent and position, Wenwei in ritual and ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: The Wen and Chen clans in talent and rank; Dou Wenwei in ritual and ceremony.

sentences.zh: 諸竇戚裡，榮盛無比。

translations.literal: The various Dou as affinal kin—in glory and flourishing none could compare.
translations.idiomatic: The Dou clan as imperial kin—none could match their glory.
